mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance, which lowers discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows falls below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 4.5% for two consecutive months, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered periods, or average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, triggering a sell-off in equities that produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decline > 0.5% and RSAFS decline > 0.5% in same month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline >0.5%, or Rank IC over 3-year windows falls below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: During manufacturing contraction (INDPRO < 100), supply chain disruptions reduce corporate profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO < 100, or Rank IC over 3-year windows falls below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: Strong employment growth (PAYEMS increase > 0.3% month-over-month) consistently supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods with PAYEMS growth > 0.3%, or Rank IC over 3-year windows falls below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When year-over-year CPI inflation exceeds 3.5%, it signals persistent inflation that prompts restrictive monetary policy, depressing equity valuations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered periods, or average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) and monthly housing starts (HOUST) indicate a severe economic slowdown, triggering risk-off sentiment that produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 decline > 0.5% YoY and HOUST decline > 0.5% MoM
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both GDPC1 declines >0.5% YoY and HOUST declines >0.5% MoM, or Rank IC over 3-year windows falls below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and rising), higher real interest rates reduce the present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and rising, or Rank IC over 3-year windows falls below 0.02.
